name: uses a deterministic local seed without changing NumPy global state
input: two runs over a separable two-cluster dataset
test:
import numpy as np
X = np.array([[1.0, 1.0], [2.0, 2.0], [8.0, 8.0], [9.0, 9.0]])
np.random.seed(12345)
expected_next = np.random.random()
np.random.seed(12345)
first_centroids, first_labels = kmeans(X, 2, 20, seed=7)
actual_next = np.random.random()
second_centroids, second_labels = kmeans(X, 2, 20, seed=7)
assert np.isclose(actual_next, expected_next)
assert np.array_equal(first_centroids, second_centroids)
assert np.array_equal(first_labels, second_labels)
assert first_centroids.shape == (2, 2)
assert first_labels.shape == (4,)

name: keeps empty centroids finite and labels consistent with returned centroids
input: duplicate input rows with more centroids than occupied groups
test:
import numpy as np
X = np.array([[3.0, -1.0], [3.0, -1.0], [3.0, -1.0]])
centroids, labels = kmeans(X, 3, 5, seed=2)
assert centroids.shape == (3, 2)
assert labels.shape == (3,)
assert np.isfinite(centroids).all()
assert np.array_equal(labels, np.argmin(((X[:, None, :] - centroids[None, :, :]) ** 2).sum(axis=2), axis=1))

name: returns labels for the final centroids after one update
input: a one-dimensional dataset with a single update
test:
import numpy as np
X = np.array([[0.0], [0.1], [9.9], [10.0]])
centroids, labels = kmeans(X, 2, 1, seed=1)
expected = np.argmin(((X[:, None, :] - centroids[None, :, :]) ** 2).sum(axis=2), axis=1)
assert np.array_equal(labels, expected)
assert set(labels.tolist()) == {0, 1}
assert np.allclose(np.sort(centroids[:, 0]), [0.05, 9.95])
